name: Clean the Customer List
description: A merged customer export from two systems (membership and class bookings) for a leisure centre: nicknames, Mc/Mac, typos, swapped first and last names, moves to a new address, a shared office email used by different people, the same name at a different company, a married-name change confirmed by phone and date of birth, a father and son at one address, and +44/07 phone formats. Exact matching rules are stated (including staff notes and “gone away” records); the answer is the grouping of records into customers plus each group’s surviving master record and golden email and phone. Groups are marked pair by pair (pairwise F1), so merging everything or nothing scores close to zero.
hook: Merge the duplicates in a messy customer list by the rules, without merging different people.
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 60 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

Reply with one JSON object:
{
  "clusters": [["M-10001", "B-20002"], ["..."]],
  "golden": { "M-10001": { "email": "name@example.com", "phone": "07700900123" } }
}
clusters: every group of two or more records that are the same customer (leave out records with no duplicate). golden: one entry per group, keyed by the group's surviving master record id. Give exactly one value for every field: alternatives, ranges or "either/or" answers are marked wrong. Groups are marked pair by pair (every pair of records correctly put together counts, every wrong pair costs); golden entries are marked as a set keyed by master id (an entry under a wrong id costs as much as a missing one), and each email and phone is checked.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 100 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 130 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 160 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 180 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 200 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 210 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 220 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.

From: Hollie Barker (Membership Manager, Kirklees Fitness & Swim)
Subject: Customer list clean-up before the new CRM goes live

Hi, before we move to the new CRM we need to merge duplicate customers. The export below combines MemberHub (ids M-...) and the BookIt class-booking app (ids B-...): 520 records. Please group the records that are the same customer using exactly the rules below, and tell me which record survives in each group.

MATCHING RULES
Name comparison: ignore capitals, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops. Surnames starting "Mac" and "Mc" are the same (MacLeod = McLeod). Surnames also match if, after the clean-up above, they differ by exactly one letter added, removed or changed and both are at least 5 letters long (a typo). First names match only if they are the same or are listed together in the nickname table. A record whose first-name and last-name fields are swapped counts as having the names in the right order.
Nickname table: Robert = Bob = Rob = Bobby; William = Bill = Will; Elizabeth = Liz = Beth = Lizzie; Katherine = Kate = Kathy; Michael = Mike; James = Jim = Jamie; David = Dave; Anthony = Tony; Margaret = Maggie = Peggy; Jonathan = Jon; Alexander = Alex; Christopher = Chris; Thomas = Tom; Daniel = Dan; Rebecca = Becky = Becca; Victoria = Vicky = Tori; Patrick = Paddy; Abdullah = Abdul; Mohammed = Mo; Oluwaseun = Seun; Aleksandra = Ola.
Phones: compare digits only, and treat a leading +44 as 0 (+44 7700 900123 = 07700 900123 = 07700900123). Emails: ignore capitals. Postcodes: ignore capitals and spaces. Address line: ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.
Shared mailboxes: an email address whose part before the @ is one of office, info, accounts, admin, reception, hello, enquiries, bookings, hr, team is a shared mailbox and never links records on its own.
Two records are the same customer if ANY of these holds:
  R1. Same email address (not a shared mailbox) and matching first names.
  R2. Same phone number and matching first names and surnames.
  R3. Same date of birth and matching first names and surnames.
  R4. Same phone number and same date of birth and matching first names (surnames may differ, e.g. after marriage).
  R5. Matching first names and surnames, the same postcode and the same address line.
Block: two records that both have a date of birth, with different dates, are never the same customer, whatever else matches.
Records linked through a chain of matching pairs are all one customer (if A matches B and B matches C, then A, B and C are one customer). A blank field never matches anything.
Notes: a record whose notes say it is "not the same person as" another record never matches that record directly, whatever the rules say (staff checked).
Surviving master record: in each group, the record with the most recent last_activity date, but never a record with status "gone away" (post returned) unless every record in the group is gone away; if two share that date, the MemberHub record; then the lower id.
Golden record (what the new CRM keeps for each group, filled from ALL records of the group): email = the most recent non-blank email in the group that is not a shared mailbox, in lower case; phone = the most recent non-blank phone in the group, as digits only starting 0 (e.g. 07700900123). "Most recent" means latest last_activity, with the same tie-breaks as for the master. A gone-away record still counts for these. If there is none, null.
